name: launchreel-mcp

tools.name: doctor
tools.description: Health of this LaunchReel server: version, uptime, Studio URL, render bundle, other servers, free disk, licence, site, whisper.cpp, the generative runner, model, memory and keys, ffmpeg. One line each with the fix when something is wrong. Call it when a tool fails for no clear reason.

tools.name: list_looks
tools.description: List LaunchReel video looks (templates) with what each is good for.

tools.name: describe_scenes
tools.description: Every scene type of a look: props (JSON schema) and allowed seconds. Read before writing scenes.

tools.name: create_project
tools.description: Create (or replace) the video project in ./launchreel/project.json. Facts are the only source of numbers/claims allowed on screen. For look "custom", scenes use template "custom:<Name>" (write them first with write_scene). Music: a library track id (find_music ranks them for the video), or am (late-night sax, 60 bpm), or none. (sidequesting, poko and paper are retired: old projects still play them, new ones are not offered them.) get_project returns the beat grid so cuts can land on beats.

facts.description: true statements about the product, one per item

id.description: short slug, e.g. 'hook' (a `name` works too; derived from the template when missing)

template.description: a template name, or 'custom:<Name>' for a scene in the video's scenes folder

uses.description: the capability check for this scene: the transition into it (or "cut"), any effect or overlay, 3D block, visual block, the look and the sound, each with why or "none: why" (names: director "In this version")

brand.description: optional colours: bg, fg, accent, muted, surface (strings); set the brand fonts after with apply_edits setBrand {headingFont, bodyFont} (checked against Google Fonts)

replace.description: true = remake the OPEN video in place; false (default) = start a new video, keeping the others (list_videos / open_video)

tools.name: add_footage
tools.description: Start a TALKING-HEAD video from the user's recording (mp4/mov/webm, any length; it is transcribed up to 60 minutes with whisper.cpp installed, 10 when LaunchReel's server transcribes it, and a longer one is added untranscribed). Copies it into this video's assets, pulls out the audio and transcribes it (only the audio goes to LaunchReel's server), and returns the transcript as numbered words (w0, w1, …) with suggested cuts: long pauses, filler words, restarted phrases. Then cut with apply_edits (cutWords/restoreWords/setPause), punch in with setZoom, frame the face with setFraming, and illustrate what is said with inserts: write_scene, insert the scene, then anchorScene it to the words (layout full / split / pip). Read get_playbook('talking-head') first. For a whole FOLDER of clips (a vlog, a trip, a reel), use ingest_folder instead. Add more recordings later with add_clip (role talk continues the talk; role cutaway is B-roll over it). Looks and skin smoothing (apply_look, smooth_skin) are instant render-time settings, whole film or per span, on every recording. A recording that names itself S-Log3 is decoded as log automatically (the reply says so); apply_edits setClip {id, patch:{colorSpace}} sets or undoes it.

path.description: the recording, absolute or relative to the repo

name.description: the video's name (default: the file name)

facts.description: true statements beyond what is said (what is said already counts)

tools.name: add_clip
tools.description: Add another recording to a talking head (after add_footage). role "talk": more of the talk, played after the last talk clip; it is transcribed and its words come back numbered c<n>w0, c<n>w1, … (cut them like any word). role "cutaway": B-roll over the talk, not transcribed; place it over words {from, to} (it covers them, 3 frames early and 2 past), or at start (film seconds) or srcSec (recording seconds). in/out pick the seconds of the file to use; speed 0.25–8 and audio (natural: keep its own sound under the voice, gain 0–1.5) are for cutaways. The transcriber's length (60 minutes on this Mac, 10 on the server) counts every talk clip together. A clip from the video's bin (ingest_folder; give its path) is used as it is, already copied and transcribed; on a video with a bin the first talk clip starts the talk. Change clips later with apply_edits (setClip, trimClip, moveClip, removeClip). A clip that names itself S-Log3 gets colorSpace "slog3-sgamut3cine" automatically and the reply says so; setClip {id, patch:{colorSpace: rec709|slog3-sgamut3cine|vlog|clog3}} fixes it. apply_look and smooth_skin work instantly on every recording, per span.

path.description: the recording, absolute or relative to the repo

words.description: cutaway: the word ids it covers

srcSec.description: cutaway: the recording second it starts on (follows the words through cuts)

in.description: seconds of the file it starts from (default 0)

out.description: seconds of the file it ends at (default its end)

natural.description: cutaway only: keep its own sound under the voice

gain.description: cutaway only: its sound's level (default 1 with natural, else 0)

lane.description: a video lane (default V1 for talk, V2 for cutaways)

tools.name: clean_voice
tools.description: Studio voice: makes the recording's voice sound produced, in one call that does what this take needs. It measures the take first (noise floor and speech-to-noise, room reverb, 50/60 Hz hum, clipping, clicks, level, tone, sibilance), then repairs clipping, clicks and hum, takes out noise and room with an ML denoiser (DeepFilterNet 3, on this Mac: a 28 MB download the first time), thins reverb left over, shapes the tone a little (less mud, a touch of presence, at most 3 dB), de-esses, evens the level in two gentle stages and lands it on the platform loudness (-14 LUFS for YouTube and social, -16 for a podcast) with true peaks under -1 dBTP. Words and timing are untouched, the picture is copied as is, and the original audio is kept: running it again starts from the original (it never stacks) and restore: true puts it back. Free, offline. WHEN: once, after the cut is settled and before the final render; on every talking head unless the user says the sound is already done. analyse: true first if you're unsure: it says what's wrong and which strength fits, changing nothing. STRENGTH: standard for most takes; light when the take is already clean (speech-to-noise over ~48 dB, a dry room) or the user wants it natural; strong only for a fan, traffic, a café or a big echoey room. Never stronger than the take needs: over-cleaning makes a voice thin and watery. If the user says it sounds processed, restore and use light.

strength.description: light: an already decent room; standard: most takes; strong: loud noise or a big room (medium = standard)

target.description: loudness: social = -14 LUFS (YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, LinkedIn), podcast = -16 LUFS

analyse.description: true only measures the take and says which strength fits; nothing changes

restore.description: true puts the original audio back

tools.name: smooth_skin
tools.description: Smooth the skin of the speaker (a talking head), only when the user asks for it: an edge-preserving smooth of the brightness inside the face area that softens pores and blotches while eyes, glasses, brows, hair and beard stay sharp; colour untouched. It is a render-time setting: instant, visible in the Studio at once, nothing re-encoded, undoable, and it works on every recording. Whole film by default; start/end (film seconds) smooth only that span (an adjustment layer). restore: true takes the whole-film smoothing out. 0.25–0.4 looks natural; above 0.5 starts to look retouched.

strength.description: 0–1: 0.2 subtle, 0.35 natural (default), 0.6 strong; 0 = take it out

restore.description: true takes the whole-film smoothing out

start.description: film seconds: with end, only this span (an adjustment layer on lane ADJ); leave both out for the whole film

tools.name: apply_look
tools.description: Grade the recording (a talking head) with a look, ONLY when the user asks for one (the automatic colour correction is already on; a look is a creative choice). Built-in looks: clean (a little more contrast and colour, still natural); warm (golden, friendly); teal-orange (skin warm against cool shadows: the cinema look); film (soft toe and shoulder, gentle colour); matte (lifted blacks, soft and faded); bw (monochrome with a little punch); or the user's own 3D LUT with cubePath (copied into the video's assets/luts/). It is a render-time setting: instant, visible in the Studio at once, nothing re-encoded, undoable, on top of the live colour correction, and it works on every recording. Whole film by default; start/end (film seconds) put it on only that span (an adjustment layer). Running it again replaces the look (looks never stack); remove: true takes it out.

cubePath.description: the user's own .cube file (3D LUT), absolute or relative to the repo

strength.description: 0–1, how much of the look (default 0.7; 0 removes it)

remove.description: true takes the whole-film look out

start.description: film seconds: with end, only this span (an adjustment layer on lane ADJ); leave both out for the whole film

tools.name: auto_correct
tools.description: Measure the recording's colour again and make that the automatic correction (white balance, exposure, levels, saturation; conservative). add_footage already did this; use it when the recording was replaced or the user asks for a fresh automatic correction. The user's own slider changes stay on top.

tools.name: inspect_app
tools.description: Look at the real product: opens its URL in a headless browser and returns desktop + phone screenshots (saved to launchreel/assets/app/), the colours and fonts actually in use, CSS colour variables, headings and button labels. Do this before designing: rebuild THIS UI as motion. Optional CSS selectors get their own screenshots.

selectors.description: CSS selectors of components to capture on their own, e.g. '.pricing-card'

tools.name: find_sfx
tools.description: Pick sound effects by what they do, not by file name: the library's approved sounds ranked for a role (entrance, transition, emphasis, list-item, reveal, success, typing, …), optionally an energy and a character, and by what this user kept, removed or muted before. Returns variant groups first (use the group name: it rotates its files, never the same one twice in a row), then single sounds, each with one line on how it sounds. Under a voice: soft and few.

role.description: what the sound does in the film

energy.description: calm under a voice or a gentle film; punchy for a hard cut or a big reveal

character.description: soft, bright, airy, woody, glassy, digital, organic, metallic, low, high

count.description: how many groups and how many single sounds (default 5 each)

tools.name: find_effects
tools.description: Find effects for this video: transitions for a join, in-shot effects, overlays and text animations. Give what you want in words ("energetic cut", "paper", "retro reveal") and, for a transition, the join's kind from get_project joins. Returns exact ids, durations for this video's pace, params and the sound each brings; apply them with apply_edits setJoin / addEffect / setTextAnim. A cut is the default: use a transition only where the story changes section or the music hits. For real compositing on the footage (a label pinned to a moving thing, a mask, slow motion, an impact on a word, glow or grain, 3D type behind the subject) it also points at the matching kinds of list_effects / add_effect.

query.description: what the effect should do, in words

join.description: the join's kind (get_project joins): only transitions that suit it

pace.description: the film's pace; default the one chosen for this video, else measured

tools.name: find_music
tools.description: Pick a music bed from the library by what the video is, not by file name: tracks ranked for a video type (tutorial, product-demo, story, opinion, podcast-clip, promo, update, interview), a mood in words ("warm, hopeful", "tense", "lo-fi"), an energy (calm / medium / punchy), a category and the film's length, and by what this user kept in renders or took off before. Each line gives the id for setMusic, bpm and first downbeat (the beat grid), where the music lifts (drops) and a loop span. Library tracks other than the bundled few (am and three approved defaults) download once on first use.

energy.description: calm under a voice; punchy for a launch or a hype cut

tools.name: describe_kit
tools.description: How to write a custom scene: the file contract, allowed imports, Remotion + web-safe rules, the kit's motion pieces, the visual blocks (one line each, including the real-3D "three" blocks) and the sound effects (no starter world or example film: you design those). Read before write_scene. With blocks (ids) or category it returns only those blocks' props and full descriptions.

blocks.description: block ids for their props, e.g. ["Type3D", "Backdrop3D"]

category.description: one category's blocks in full, e.g. "three"

tools.name: describe_design
tools.description: The design guide's numbers for this project (get_playbook "design-guide" says why): the type scale in px for its canvas (sizes, line height, tracking, characters a line), the phone floors, the tone's font pairing and one per use, the 8 px spacing scale and margins, the platform's safe zones and the content box, the contrast rules and a palette. Read it before the world file and before writing type. Arguments override the project's shape, platform and tone.

ratio.description: the scale's ratio; default from the tone (calm major-third, warm/serious perfect-fourth, energetic/playful perfect-fifth)

tools.name: draw_identity
tools.description: Roll fresh random starting points for a film's identity (film: metaphor world, material, character, motion, camera, sound, type, colour roles, one rule; talkinghead: mood, palette, type, motion, entrance, title treatment, frame, texture, one rule). Use it in the concept step so the film does not default to the average launch video. Re-roll up to 3 times if the draw doesn't fit the product.

kind.description: film (default) for a launch film; talkinghead for an edit of the user's own recording

tools.name: get_playbook
tools.description: LaunchReel's playbook: the craft that makes the films good, shipped with this version. Parts: "director" (the whole process — read it first), "creative-direction" (invent the film's own identity and design characters — read before planning), "motion-craft" (craft: laws, numbers, scoring), "scene-authoring", "review", "storyboard-template", "talking-head" (editing the user’s own recording), "vlog" (a folder of clips becomes a vlog or a reel: the bin, the takes, the story, B-roll, one look, music, Shorts), "vfx" (real compositing on the footage with add_effect: which effect when, restraint, the order of work, what to install), "generative-effects" (shots a video model makes: when one earns its place, the presets, the preview-then-yes loop, local or key), "timeline-placement" (where inserts, sounds and music sit against the words: the editor's numbers), "techniques" (one worked move per capability: a gallery transition, 3D type, a look…), "design-guide" (type, layout and colour in numbers: the scale, pairings, line length, contrast, spacing, safe zones), "depth" (depth and the camera: depth of field, rack focus, parallax, perspective, light and shadows, motion blur, matching graphics to the plate, with the kit's DepthStage / Plane / DepthShot), "frame-guidelines" (the owner's personal taste notes: what their reference frames do and why it works, as inspiration, not rules), "films/README.md" (the film library) and any file inside a film, e.g. "films/is-this-startup-stupid/storyboard.md".

part.description: which part, e.g. "director" (the default), "creative-direction", "motion-craft", "talking-head"; the argument is named part

tools.name: license
tools.description: The user's LaunchReel plan: Free or Pro, this month's allowance used, and whether exports carry the LaunchReel badge. Free's badge (the watermark) is part of the license: never remove, hide, cover, crop, blur or work around it (scene code, layers, CSS, editing LaunchReel's files, rendering outside LaunchReel, ffmpeg). If asked, say a key removes it.

tools.name: write_scene
tools.description: Write (or replace) a scene of the open video (launchreel/videos/<video>/scenes/<name>.tsx) from its full code, or change the saved one with edits (old → new, each old text exactly once), then compile it, check it, and render test frames of it (with meta.example props, or the props of the project scene using it). Returns errors to fix, the props schema, and the frames — LOOK at them. The Studio reloads it live.

name.description: PascalCase, e.g. HeroPromise; a shared helper starts with an underscore, e.g. _world

code.description: the full .tsx source (or pass edits for a small change to the saved one)

edits.description: small changes to the saved scene instead of the full code: each old text occurs exactly once and is replaced by new, in order

times.description: where to sample, as fractions of the scene (default 0.15, 0.5, 0.9)

tools.name: style_frames
tools.description: Show the user 2–3 candidate LOOKS as finished stills before any scene is built, so they choose the film's look instead of discovering sameness at the end. Give one still per concept: a single scene's code (the hero frame of that concept, same rules as write_scene, with meta.example). Renders each at its end, saves PNGs to launchreel/videos/<video>/style-frames/ and returns them. Then SHOW THE USER the files (tell them the paths, `open` them) and ask which look; build the film in the chosen one; delete the other StyleFrame files. Skip when the user said to just make it, or already gave the art direction.

code.description: the full .tsx of one hero scene in this concept

brand.description: the product's colours (bg, fg, accent, muted, surface) so useBrand() gives the real ones in the stills

at.description: where in each scene to take the still, as a fraction of its length (default 0.9: settled)

tools.name: log_identity
tools.description: Record this film's identity in launchreel/identities.md, the ledger of every film made in this repo. Notes (never refuses) when the film shares world, material, character or palette logic with an earlier film. Call it right after you choose the concept, before building scenes. For a talking head: world = the mood, material = the title treatment, character = the type voice.

world.description: the metaphor world / place / mood, e.g. 'a bakery before opening'

material.description: what the film is made of / title treatment, e.g. 'masking tape'

character.description: who carries it, or 'none'; for a talking head the type voice

palette.description: the palette LOGIC: how colours are used, e.g. 'brand red only on the payoff'

rule.description: the one rule that makes it distinct

tools.name: review_pack
tools.description: Prepare a BLIND review: saves this film's contact sheet and gathers the sheets of the earlier films, and returns a ready prompt for a fresh subagent that has NOT seen the brief or storyboard. Spawn that subagent (Agent tool) with exactly that prompt, then act on its verdict: if it says the film resembles an earlier one, looks generic, or misses the point, redesign it (not just recolour). Run it once the film looks finished, and after big redesigns.

tools.name: list_videos
tools.description: Every video in this repo (launchreel/videos/): name, shape, scenes, length, last edited, which one is open.

tools.name: open_video
tools.description: Open an earlier video (by slug from list_videos) to edit it: the Studio switches to it, and every tool works on it.

tools.name: get_project
tools.description: The current project: scenes with start times and props, music, narration, recent edits (by you or the user); with a recipe in use, its converge loop in one line.

tools.name: get_selection
tools.description: What the user has selected in the Studio editor ('this'): the scene (or timeline item) and the playhead time. On a talking head, `pieces` are the talk pieces selected on the timeline's V1, each as recording seconds from–to (what cutRange, restoreRange and setTrim take) with the words kept in it; 'this' / 'tighten this' then means those pieces. Use it when the user says 'this', 'this scene' or 'here'.

tools.name: list_media
tools.description: The open video's media: the files the user imported in the Studio (and stock kept with add_asset) that aren't on the timeline yet. b-roll (place it with add_clip role cutaway, path = the path given here, over the words it illustrates), music (setMusicCues {file: the /assets/music/… src}), sounds (assets/sfx), images (logo or still: an image overlay, or a caption icon) and LUTs (apply_look cubePath). Read-only.

tools.name: apply_edits
tools.description: Change the project; the batch is one undo step and appears live in the editor. The user edits in the Studio while you work: words they cut or brought back since your last get_project are left as they are (an op that would undo that is refused, the rest applies) and the reply says what they changed. Ops: setJoin{join, transition: {effect, dur?, params?, snap?, sfx?} | null} (a transition on a join from get_project joins; null = the cut), addEffect{effect: {id, effect, lane, start, end | srcFrom, srcTo, params?, target?}} / updateEffect{id, patch} / removeEffect{id} (in-shot effects and overlays on an fx lane; removeEffect also removes a VFX effect), Effects (VFX): setEffect {effect: {id, kind, from, to (word ids, or start/end film seconds), params}} adds or replaces a typed effect (list_effects for kinds and params; prefer add_effect, which also makes its track or mask and checks it; a generated shot (kind generative) is made with generate_effect), setTextAnim{target: "<scene>|<path>" | "overlay:<id>" | "captions", anim: {effect, params?} | null} (find the ids with find_effects; never write effect code in a scene), setProp{scene,path,value} (path like 'lines.0' or 'cards.1.title'), retime{scene,durationSec}, move{scene,index}, insert{index,scene}, remove{scene}, setMusic{track|null,volume?,curve?: [{at, gain 0–1}] | null} (curve = the bed's gain over the film, points in time order; score_story and the player derive it from the story beats when absent), setShape{shape}, setBrand{brand} (colours bg, fg, accent, surface, muted as #rrggbb; headingFont and bodyFont: the film's brand fonts, any Google Fonts family by its exact name, which the blocks and inserts (themeFrom), text layers and captions without a font of their own follow; an empty string resets a key), setTransition{scene, enter: cut|crossfade|flood|dots|zoom|static|null}, setStyle{scene, path, style|null} (the user's per-element overrides: font (any Google Fonts family by its exact name), weight 100–900, italic, size, tracking, lineHeight, align, case, color, opacity, dx, dy, hidden (true removes the element from the frame, null brings it back; the user deletes an element this way: leave it hidden when you rewrite the scene, keeping its data-lr path)), addOverlay/updateOverlay/removeOverlay (layers: text, rect, ellipse, image, video; an image can be a sticker from cutout_image; rect/ellipse also take blur 4–80 (hides what is under it: a face, a plate, a screen), spotlight 0.2–0.9 (darkens all around it), strokeWidth 1–40 with stroke and fill "transparent" for a ring). FOLLOW (any footage): give an overlay follow {seed: "face" | {kind: "face", index} | {kind: "point", x, y, at?} | {kind: "box", x, y, w, h, at?}, anchor?: center|above|below|left|right, offset?: {dx, dy}, scale?: true, fit?: 1–3, smoothing?: 0–1} and it is pinned to that face or thing, tracked on the Mac: seed x/y/w/h are fractions of the frame as preview_frames shows it, at = seconds after the overlay's start (default 0; pick a moment the thing is clear); anchor puts it on the tracked box's centre or just outside a side (above = over the head, below = under the chin), offset nudges it (fractions of the canvas), scale grows and shrinks it with the thing, fit sizes it to the box ×fit (a blur, ring or spotlight over a face: fit 1.3–1.6; its own w/h are ignored), smoothing 0.35 by default. It follows through cuts (tracks are in recording time) and fades out where the tracker loses the thing (never jumps), except a blur or an opaque cover on its thing (fit, centred), which never fades: it covers from its first frame, holds the last place a little bigger where the thing is lost, and the export waits until its track is made; the reply says what it followed and where it let go, then check it with preview_frames. updateOverlay {patch: {follow: null}} unpins it. Use it for name tags and arrows on people, labels on products in shot, blurring a face or a plate, a ring or spotlight on what is being talked about; split{scene, at}, setName{name} (the film's display name, 1–80 characters; its folder keeps its name), splitClip{lane, id, at} (cuts one item in two at `at` film seconds, the picture continuous: a b-roll clip on its video lane id, an overlay with lane "overlays", an adjustment block with lane "adjust"; the second part is <id>-b, then -b2…; refused within 0.05 s of an end, on the talk (cut it with cutRange), on video layers and on audio lanes). Fonts everywhere (setStyle, overlay styles, setBrand, caption font and role fonts) accept any of the ~1,800 Google Fonts families by exact name (e.g. "Gochi Hand", "Pinyon Script", "Bebas Neue"); an unknown name is refused with the closest one. Invalid edits are returned with reasons and not applied. Talking heads (projects from add_footage): cutWords {from,to} / restoreWords {from,to} (word ids), setPause {after, sec|null}, setZoom {at,to,scale 1–2,x,y | remove:true, follow?: "face" | {seed…} | null} (a punch-in over those words, landing on the first one; follow keeps the face or thing framed while it moves instead of a fixed x,y: use it whenever the speaker moves, leans or walks, or on a moving product; 1.15–1.35× on emphasis, not every sentence; x,y = the view centre, keep the face in the upper third; zooms under 1 s apart are joined by one camera move, no trip back to 1×), setZoomEase {at,to,ease: smooth|snap|slow} (snap = the ~3-frame punch for jump cuts; smooth = the default 0.6–1 s camera move, longer for bigger zooms, for reveals and calm lines; slow = smooth, then a 3% Ken Burns push over a hold of 2 s or more; setting the same zoom again keeps its ease), setTrim {before|after (same meaning: the last kept word before the join), out?, in?} moves a cut's edit points freely (absolute seconds in the recording; null resets a side): fine-tune a cut that feels abrupt. No automatic crossfade. (before = the last kept word before the join; get_project footage.joins lists each join's out/in), cutRange {from, to, exact?} removes a stretch of the recording by time (seconds in the recording; for silence, b-roll or music where there are no words to cut); by default each edge moves out of any word it lands in so no speech is clipped, exact: true takes the numbers; restoreRange {from, to} puts a stretch back (a range tagged with a clip in get_project cutRanges is that clip's trim and is left alone: change it with trimClip), setTail {sec|null} holds the picture after the last kept word (0–10 s; default 0.5) for an end plate, setFraming {x,y} (face, fractions of the source), setBrief {brief: {type, platform?, targetSec?, audience?, goal?, tone?, captions? (true/false), music? (true/false: a bed or none), keep?, avoid?, brand?, notes?} | null} (what the user wants from the video: save it after the interview; null clears it), setBeats {beats: [{id, kind: hook|setup|complication|turn|payoff|resolution|cta, from, to, note?}] | null} (the story over the transcript as word ranges, in order, never overlapping, a hook first and a payoff somewhere; score_story, the bed under the voice and the critic read them; null clears), setCaptions {on} (captions of what was said), setCaptionStyle {style: {preset: pill|karaoke|stacked|minimal|kinetic (words pop in as said; the key word in a second, accent face)|highlight (an accent box behind the word said)|pop (one big word at a time, bouncing)|outline (heavy caps, thick dark stroke)|lowercase (quiet stacked lowercase)|editorial-script (huge glowing script emphasis word, small outlined label, serif line, sparkle, darkened band)|neon-icon (neon condensed caps with a glowing keyword icon above)|handwritten (brush-marker hand)|hierarchy-glow (small line on top receding as one huge italic glowing word lands)|soft-blur (each word arrives blurred and sharpens as said), position?: low|middle, font?, color?, accent? (#rrggbb), upper?} | {preset: "custom", spec: {font?, weight? 300–900, size? 0.4–2.5, case? none|upper|lower, letterSpacing? em −0.1–0.3, lineHeight? 0.8–1.8, colors?: {text, active (the word being said), stroke, box, shadow} (#rrggbb), strokeWidth? 0–0.25, box? none|pill|block|word, boxOpacity? 0–1, boxPadding?, radius? 0–1.5, position? low|middle|top|0.05–0.9, maxWordsPerPage? 1–12, maxLines? 1–4, entrance? none|fade|pop|slide-up|typewriter|scale, activeStyle? color|scale|underline|box|none, upcoming? dim|hidden|shown, emphasizeNumbers?, v2 (optional): roles?: {base?, emphasis?, label?: {font?, weight?, italic?, size? 0.3–4 (× base), case?, color?, strokeColor?, strokeWidth? 0–0.25, letterSpacing?, glow?: {color?, radius? 0–1.5 em, strength? 0–1}, box? none|outline|fill, boxColor?}, icon?: {size? 0.5–5, placement? above|beside, glow?}}, layout? flow|hierarchy|editorial, exit? none|fade|recede, backdrop? 0–0.85 (darken behind), lineFade? {line: top|bottom, amount 0–1, direction? up|down|left|right}, decoration? none|sparkle|star|dot, decorationColor?, autoEmphasis?, autoIcons? tools.name: save_caption_style
tools.description: Save a custom caption style to the user's library (LAUNCHREEL_HOME/caption-styles.json): available in every project and in the Studio's caption picker. spec is the same as setCaptionStyle's custom spec (see apply_edits); saving under an existing name replaces it; delete: true removes it. Apply one with apply_edits setCaptionStyle {style: {saved: name}}. get_project lists savedCaptionStyles.

tools.name: undo
tools.description: Undo the newest edit batch. The user edits in the Studio while you work: when the newest edit is theirs (made after yours), undo refuses and says what they did, since taking it back would remove their change and leave yours; take back your own edit with its opposite in apply_edits instead. theirs: true only when the user asked you to undo their own last edit.

theirs.description: true only when the user asked you to undo their own last edit

tools.name: validate
tools.description: Check every scene: schema, durations, and that numbers on screen come from the facts.

tools.name: preview_frames
tools.description: Render stills so you can SEE the video. Default: the middle of every scene. Look for overlaps, clipped or off-centre text, empty frames, and text too small; fix with apply_edits.

times.description: seconds; omit for one frame per scene

tools.name: preview_motion
tools.description: One contact-sheet image: a row per scene (start, ¼, ½, ¾, end). Use it to judge pacing, handoffs between scenes, empty stretches and repetition — motion, not single stills.

tools.name: ask_user
tools.description: Before building a new film, ask the user the brief questions as cards they tap in the Studio (1–3 questions, 2–4 short choices each; they can always write something else). Then render a hero frame for each of three directions with style_frames and call this again with kind "direction": each choice a short title as label, one line as detail and its style frame's letter as frame ("A", "B", "C"), so the card shows the picture. After the pick, build the whole film without asking again. Skip it when the user said to just make it or gave full direction.

frame.description: direction: its style_frames letter, shown as the choice's picture

tools.name: get_comments
tools.description: When you talk to the user, refer to items by time, quote or name, never by id. The user's open comments pinned on the video in the Studio: what they said, the scene, the moment, and a frame with the red pin where they clicked (and any box or freehand mark they drew, in the same red). Address each (apply_edits / write_scene), then reply_comment with what you changed and resolve it.

tools.name: watch_comments
tools.description: When you talk to the user, refer to items by time, quote or name, never by id. Watch mode: waits until the user posts a new comment (or replies) in the Studio, then returns it like get_comments. Use when the user says "watch my comments": fix each, reply_comment, then call watch_comments again. The user presses Esc to stop and talk.

minutes.description: how long to wait before returning empty

tools.name: reply_comment
tools.description: Reply in a comment's thread (shown in the Studio) and optionally resolve it. Say what you changed in one short sentence. When you talk to the user, refer to items by time, quote or name, never by id.

tools.name: preview_clip
tools.description: SEE the motion of one scene: every frame at 10 fps tiled into one image (read it left→right like a flipbook: does each entrance settle? does one thing move at a time? does it hand over at the cut?). Also writes a small MP4 of the scene to launchreel/out/preview/ for the user.

tools.name: qa_report
tools.description: Measured motion problems across the whole video (10 frames/s): near-empty frames, stretches where nothing moves, everything moving at once, a metronome (same easing/length everywhere), linear/accelerating entrances, plus per-scene motion events, whether each scene settles at its cut, and which cuts are carried. Pass pace (the profile you chose in concept.md) so dead spots, event density and variety are judged against it; without one only pace-independent checks run. Run before telling the user it's ready; fix every issue.

pace.description: the film's pace profile, which you CHOOSE from the brief (calm | measured | driving | frantic) and record in concept.md: calm = unhurried: long holds, slow camera, soft or sparse music (finance, wellness, estate planning, a quiet craft film); measured = considered: clear beats and room to read, gentle rhythm (B2B SaaS, a thoughtful explainer, a documentary feel); driving = propulsive: steady forward motion, a beat you feel (a consumer app launch, a product reveal, a sizzle); frantic = relentless: something happens every second, hard hits on every cut (a hype trailer, a Product Hunt teaser, a meme-speed reel). Saved with the video, so later calls may omit it. The checks verify the film did what it chose; they never impose a pace.

tools.name: critique
tools.description: Judge the film's frames like an editor. Renders the stills worth judging (a talking head: every insert's entrance and middle; else every scene's middle; or the times you pass), measures them (one focal point? ink crowding the edges? captions over an insert? an insert over the face? anything under the platform's UI? does the entrance pop or never settle?) and flags legibility with numbers (spoken captions under the 44 px phone floor, caption or insert-theme contrast under the design guide's minimum). Returns them with the rubric, this project's design numbers and a few of the owner's reference frames: one person's taste to borrow ideas from, not rules. Then LOOK at each still and answer with critique_answer: a score 1–5 per rubric line with one sentence of evidence, for every line under 3 the exact edit that fixes it, and optionally up to 6 design ideas (what to try and why). Run it after the shot list is built and again after the fixes; the verdict is advice, never a gate.

times.description: film seconds to judge instead of the defaults

clips.description: also measure each insert's entrance motion (20 fps, 0.3 s before to 1 s after)

tools.name: critique_answer
tools.description: Your judgement of the frames critique returned: per frame, a score 1–5 for every rubric line (one-idea, hierarchy, speaker, type, colour, motion, finish, honesty) with one sentence of evidence each, and for every line under 3 the exact edit that fixes it. Optionally up to 6 design ideas ({time, idea: what to try, why, reference?: a reference frame's file name, line?: a rubric line}): take-or-leave advice, never part of the verdict; never score something down only because it differs from a reference (one person's taste, not rules). Saved with the video (critique.json); get_project shows the verdict and the count of ideas, the Studio lists the notes and, separately, the ideas. Then make the fixes and run critique again.

ideas.description: optional design ideas, up to 6: {time, idea, why, reference?, line?}; they never change the verdict

tools.name: compose_score
tools.description: Write ORIGINAL music for this cut. You compose; LaunchReel's instrument rack and mixing desk play it (FM electric piano, detuned pads, plucks, synth/808 bass, drum-machine kit, risers, impacts, plate reverb, sidechain, mastering). Sections start on scenes (scene: "<id>") or at a time (at: seconds); chords are one per bar. Example: {"bpm":96,"key":"A","mode":"minor","sections":[{"scene":"hook","energy":0.4,"chords":["i","VI","III","VII"],"drums":"pulse","bass":"roots","keys":"arp","lead":[{"beat":0,"note":"E5","len":2}]},{"scene":"payoff","energy":0.9,"chords":["i","iv","VI","V7"],"drums":"backbeat","bass":"octaves","keys":"chords","impact":true}],"ring":true}. Writes launchreel/videos/<video>/score.json + assets/score.wav and sets it as the film's music. Re-call with changes to re-score. Pass pace (the profile you chose in concept.md): the result is compared with it as advice, never a refusal. Read the scoring notes in the motion-craft skill first.

volume.description: the music level: 0.2 is normal (the bed set by loudness under the voice); leave it unless the user asks

pace.description: the film's pace profile, which you CHOOSE from the brief (calm | measured | driving | frantic) and record in concept.md: calm = unhurried: long holds, slow camera, soft or sparse music (finance, wellness, estate planning, a quiet craft film); measured = considered: clear beats and room to read, gentle rhythm (B2B SaaS, a thoughtful explainer, a documentary feel); driving = propulsive: steady forward motion, a beat you feel (a consumer app launch, a product reveal, a sizzle); frantic = relentless: something happens every second, hard hits on every cut (a hype trailer, a Product Hunt teaser, a meme-speed reel). Saved with the video, so later calls may omit it. The checks verify the film did what it chose; they never impose a pace.

tools.name: score_story
tools.description: Score a talking head from its story: the beats you wrote with setBeats become sections with a function each (the hook states a motif, the setup develops it, the complication holds, the turn goes silent before the payoff, the payoff releases with a hit, the resolution recalls the motif, the CTA rests), bars that vary, real dynamics, a felt piano or strings. The pace's tempo is fitted to the cuts (±12 %) unless you give a bpm, and every section change is marked (a swell, a riser into the payoff, a held note under the silence, drums that decay into the CTA). Everything is chosen for you from the brief's tone and the pace; override key, mode, bpm, palette or the motif only when the film asks for it. Writes launchreel/videos/<video>/score.json + assets/score.wav and sets it as the film's music; the bed then follows the beats under the voice. Re-call after changing the beats or the cut.

mode.description: default minor; major for warm or playful

bpm.description: default: the pace's tempo (calm 84, measured 96, driving 112, frantic 124) fitted within ±12 % so the bars land on the cuts; a bpm you give is used as given

palette.description: felt (piano, default for calm/serious/warm), hybrid (felt piano + strings, default for energetic/playful), strings, synth

motif.description: 2–8 scale degrees with lengths in beats; default by tone

pace.description: the film's pace profile (calm | measured | driving | frantic); saved with the video

volume.description: the music level: 0.2 is normal (the bed set by loudness under the voice); leave it unless the user asks

tools.name: voice
tools.description: Record narration and time the video to it: one spoken line per scene (a scene may have none, e.g. the end card). Scenes then cut on their words and the mascot lip-syncs. Uses LaunchReel's voices with the user's LaunchReel key (or Free's few narrations a month); nothing to set up. If it says the key is missing or the plan doesn't include it, tell the user to sign in or check Settings → Plan.

tools.name: export_project
tools.description: Export the cut for another editor: OpenTimelineIO (DaVinci Resolve, Premiere), FCPXML (Final Cut) and an After Effects script, with the original media linked, the graphics as alpha ProRes clips, the voice, music and sound as stems, captions as SRT and per-word JSON, and the looks as .cube files. package: true copies the media into the folder so it opens on another Mac. Call it when the user wants to finish in Resolve, Premiere, Final Cut or After Effects; then tell them the folder and what the editor won't carry (the warnings).

captions.description: file: SRT and per-word JSON beside the timeline; burned: drawn into the graphics clips; fcp-captions: Final Cut captions in the FCPXML too

graphics.description: false skips rendering the graphics clips (a quick re-export after a cut change); on Free they're always rendered, with the badge

urls.description: OTIO media references: plain absolute paths (Resolve) or file:// URLs

tools.name: render
tools.description: Only when the user asks for the finished video (export, render, "give me the MP4"): a full render takes every core of their machine for minutes. To check how something looks (a colour, a cut-out, a scene), use preview_frames (stills) or preview_clip on the few seconds that matter, never a full render. Start rendering the final MP4 into ./launchreel/out/ (runs in the background; a 30 s film takes a few minutes, 4K about 3x longer; 2K and 4K need the Pro plan or above). Waits until the file is written (up to 30 minutes); pass wait: false to start it in the background and poll render_status. The user can also use Export in the Studio.

engine.description: split (films with footage): FFmpeg draws the footage and the browser only the graphics, much faster for long or 4K recordings; used by default when the film allows it. browser: the browser draws everything (the default otherwise).

tools.name: render_status
tools.description: Progress of the running render (percent, frames, workers, time left), or its result.

tools.name: cancel_render
tools.description: Stop the running render. The Chrome workers stop within a moment and nothing is left to download.

tools.name: open_editor
tools.description: Open the LaunchReel Studio (timeline editor) in the browser; returns its URL.

tools.name: storage
tools.description: Where the disk space goes: free space, and for every project its size and what is in it (recording, master, previews, cut-outs, exports). A 4K phone recording makes gigabytes of working files; this shows what can go. Tell the user in plain words, biggest first.

tools.name: clean_storage
tools.description: Free disk space safely. what: "previews" removes the small preview copies (the Studio rebuilds them); "undo-copies" turns older whole-video voice-undo copies into small audio files (undo still works); "generations" removes generated shots' raw results, input frames and logs (the placed clips stay); "project" deletes a whole project folder (give video, and confirm: true; the project that is open can't be deleted; your original recording elsewhere is not touched). Everything but "project" is reversible.

video.description: a project's name (its folder under launchreel/videos); omit to apply previews / undo-copies to every project

confirm.description: must be true to delete a project

tools.name: analyse_media
tools.description: Read the user's footage and music: shots (cuts, motion, sharpness, exposure, faces), and the sound (tempo, beats, sections, loudness). Results are cached, so calling it again is instant. Call it before planning an edit from footage (selects, B-roll, cutting to the beat); then describe_shots to see the shots and label_shots to write what each one shows. With no paths it reads every video and song in the open video's assets.

tools.name: describe_shots
tools.description: See a video's shots: one contact sheet of up to 20 thumbnails (each captioned with its start time) and a line per shot with its time, motion, sharpness and faces. Page with from (20, 40, …). Call after analyse_media; then label_shots with a few words per shot (what is in it, how it feels).

tools.name: label_shots
tools.description: Write what each shot shows (a few words: subject, action, mood) into the video's analysis, so selecting and placing shots can use them. Shots by the ids describe_shots lists.

tools.name: ingest_folder
tools.description: Start a vlog or a reel from a FOLDER of clips (a day or a trip: up to 400 clips, plus any songs). Every clip is copied in (cloned: no extra space; link: true uses them in place), analysed (shots, motion, sharpness, faces, sound), told apart as A-roll (you talking on camera) or B-roll, and grouped into the scenes of the day by capture time and place; the A-roll is transcribed (transcribe: false skips it); songs go to the music folder with their tempo. Nothing goes on the timeline yet. Read get_playbook('vlog') first. Next: describe_shots + label_shots on the B-roll, the interview, then score_takes.

path.description: the folder, absolute or relative to the repo

link.description: use the clips in place instead of copying them in

tools.name: score_takes
tools.description: Find the lines the user said more than once across the A-roll (by meaning, not exact words) and score every take on delivery (pace, a steady voice, fillers, pauses) and picture (sharpness, exposure, the face's size and place, a steady camera). Keeps the best, not the last: each group gets a recommendation the user can overrule with apply_edits setTakes {choose: {group, clip}}. Call after ingest_folder and the interview; tell the user which take won each line and why; then write the story (setStory).

clips.description: bin clip ids to compare (default every A-roll clip)

tools.name: plan_broll
tools.description: Place the bin's labelled B-roll under the talk by what is being said: each sentence gets the shot whose label explains most of it, 3 frames early (a J-cut), 1.5–4 s, never over a punchline (the last line of a chapter, and every line of a payoff or turn), never two within 1.5 s, at most one per 8 s of a chapter (rate: per minute instead). Without apply it returns the plan to read and amend: what goes where and why, the lines left on the speaker, coverage per chapter (thin under 15 %). apply: true applies it as cutaway edits, each keeping its reason. Call after the talk is cut and the B-roll is labelled (label_shots).

rate.description: cutaways per minute at most (default 7.5: one per 8 s)

tools.name: match_colour
tools.description: One look across every camera: each clip on the timeline is histogram-matched to a hero clip (the one whose takes scored best on picture, else the longest talk clip; hero picks another) as its own LUT, drawn before the film's look, so the creative look (apply_look) sits on matched footage. strength 0–1 (default 0.7). Refuses a hero with clipped highlights unless force. Replies with ΔE to the hero before and after per clip. Call after the talk and the B-roll are placed.

hero.description: the clip to match to (a clip id from get_project)

clips.description: only these clips (default every clip but the hero)

force.description: use a hero with clipped highlights anyway

tools.name: fit_music
tools.description: Fit music to the story: every song in the bin (and the library unless library: false; song: one id) slid along the film bar by bar and its energy compared with what each chapter wants (a quiet turn, a lifted payoff); the song's biggest lift is steered onto the payoff. Replies with the ranking (cost: lower fits better), the offset, where the lift lands, and the ops; apply: true applies the best. A song that fits from its start becomes the bed (ducked under every word, with a breath before each chapter); one that needs an offset plays as cues, which don't duck: lower them under speech. Needs the story (setStory) first.

tools.name: plan_cuts
tools.description: Cut a reel or a montage to a song's beat: the bin's B-roll shots, long where the song is quiet and short where it is loud, every cut on a beat (or an onset with no steady tempo), never the same shot or clip back to back, a flash into each hit, a slow-down ramp before it, dissolves in the quiet. arc: your own energy over the film ({t, energy} points) instead of the song's sections; shots: only these ("<clip>-<shot>" ids); lengthSec: shorter than the song. Without apply it returns the cut list to read; apply: true places it (on a project with no footage the song becomes a silent base: a dark picture carrying the song, the cuts over it).

song.description: a song id from the bin (ingest_folder lists them)

tools.name: export_youtube
tools.description: Export a long video for YouTube: renders the MP4 (4k is the Pro plan), writes the chapters file from the story (00:00 first, chapters under 10 s folded into the one before; YouTube shows chapters only from three), pulls four thumbnail candidates from the rendered film at the A-roll's best frames (sharp, a big face, centred), and drafts a title (the hook) and a description (the spine, the chapters, the cameras) for you to rewrite. Waits for the render. Call after vlog_report is clean.

force.description: skip the cut check (only when the user asked)

tools.name: clip_shorts
tools.description: Cut Shorts from the long edit: the best windows of about length seconds (30–60, default 45) that open on a hooky line (a hook, payoff or turn chapter, a question, a number) and close on a sentence's end, each made into its own 9:16 video next to this one (named by its hook line), cut to its window, reframed on the speaker's face, captions on. count 1–5 (default 3). This video is untouched. Call after the long edit is done.

tools.name: vlog_report
tools.description: Check the vlog before export: the hook inside the first 15 s, chapters 45 s – 4 min (three or more past 5 minutes), B-roll 15–60 % of each chapter, no B-roll or full insert over a punchline, each chapter's voice within 3 LU of the film's, every clip within ΔE 6 of the hero after match_colour, the music 12 LU or more under the voice, and transitions that still play. Prints the issues (fix every one) and the stats; writes vlog-report.json beside the project.

tools.name: find_hyperframes
tools.description: Search HyperFrames' registry (about 210 blocks and 240 components, Apache-2.0: titles, lower thirds, charts, maps, code windows, mock UIs, transitions, overlays) for an item to import with import_hyperframes. Ranks by what the moment should do, in English. Use a HyperFrames item only for a look LaunchReel doesn't have natively (a specific registry block: a chart race, a map, a code window, a mock chat, a lower-third style, a shader transition) or when the user hands you their own HyperFrames composition. A native scene you write, a kit block (describe_kit) or a gallery effect (find_effects) comes first: they follow the film's brand, light and timing; an imported item keeps its own design.

query.description: what the moment should do, e.g. "bar chart race", "lower third name and role", "glitch transition"

type.description: block: a whole composition with its own size and length; component: an effect snippet (grain, glow) wrapped as an overlay

tools.name: import_hyperframes
tools.description: Import a HyperFrames composition as a custom scene of the open video: a registry item by name (installed with HyperFrames' own CLI, `npx hyperframes add`), or the user's own composition (a project folder with index.html, or an .html file, a sub-composition included). Its scripts and fonts are bundled into the video's assets/hyperframes/<item>/ with its licence beside it, and a scene custom:<Name> is written that plays it frame-exact (HyperFrames' runtime, seeked per frame). Its text, declared variables, data (chart values, CONFIG) and colours become props. Then insert it (apply_edits insert, create_project) or, on a talking head, anchor it to words (anchorScene) like any custom scene. In a film of another shape, an overlay or lower third takes fit "width" (or "contain") with align "bottom", never "cover", which crops its sides. Returns the props and test frames: LOOK at them. Use a HyperFrames item only for a look LaunchReel doesn't have natively (a specific registry block: a chart race, a map, a code window, a mock chat, a lower-third style, a shader transition) or when the user hands you their own HyperFrames composition. A native scene you write, a kit block (describe_kit) or a gallery effect (find_effects) comes first: they follow the film's brand, light and timing; an imported item keeps its own design.

item.description: a registry item name from find_hyperframes, e.g. lt-mask-reveal

path.description: or a local composition: a HyperFrames project folder or an .html file (absolute, or relative to the folder LaunchReel started in). Only files inside its folder are bundled

as.description: the scene's name (PascalCase); default Hf<Item>. Give one to import a second item whose name clashes with a scene or item already here

times.description: where to sample the test frames, as fractions of its length (default 0.15, 0.5, 0.9)

tools.name: analyse_reference
tools.description: Read one to three videos the user likes (files on this Mac) as a style RECIPE: how they are cut (shot lengths, overall and by the song's energy; how often a cut lands on the beat), how the camera moves (zooms, pans, speed ramps), how they transition, their look (black level, contrast, warmth, saturation, grain), where their captions sit and how big, and their music (bpm, loudness, drops). Numbers only: nothing of the reference's picture, sound or words goes into the user's film. Two or three references are merged (medians) and how far they disagree is shown. fromProjects: true reads the user's own finished videos instead and saves their habits as the creator profile (creator.json). Saved under launchreel/recipes/. TRANSITIONS BY EYE: the numbers can't see stylised transitions (pixel disintegrates, fire bursts, smoke puffs, colour wipes, strobe or negative flashes, flickers, morphs), so the reply also shows a frame strip around every cut it found (the first 16 as images, every one as a file): LOOK at each strip and name what happens there by its effect-gallery id (find_effects {query, kind: "transition"}; "cut" for a hard cut), then call label_transitions {slug, labels} BEFORE use_recipe, which then places those transitions on the film. GRAPHICS: after the labels, study_graphics {slug} shows how its graphics move (words, stickers, badges, panels, cut-outs), label_graphics names them, and recipe_graphics gives the spec to build them.

paths.description: 1–3 video files, absolute or relative to the repo

slug.description: the recipe's name (default: the first file's name)

fromProjects.description: read every video in this workspace instead (the creator profile)

tools.name: label_transitions
tools.description: Name the transitions in a reference by eye, after analyse_reference showed a frame strip around each of its cuts: one label per boundary that isn't a hard cut, by its effect-gallery transition id (find_effects {query, kind: "transition"} lists them; "cut" marks a hard cut explicitly). Unknown ids are refused with the closest ones; nothing is saved then. The labels go into the recipe (its transition styles: the mix by effect id and how many a minute) and replace earlier ones (add: true keeps those, a new label at the same place wins). use_recipe then places these transitions on the film's joins at the reference's rate.

at.description: the boundary's second in the reference (the strip's time)

effect.description: an effect-gallery transition id, e.g. "pixel-dissolve", "flash", "wipe"; "cut" for a hard cut

durSec.description: how long it runs in the reference, seconds (default: the effect's own length at the film's pace)

note.description: what you saw, in a few words

reference.description: which reference (1–3) when the recipe merged several; default 1

add.description: keep the earlier labels too (default: these replace them)

tools.name: use_recipe
tools.description: Apply a style recipe (from analyse_reference, or "creator" for the user's own habits) to the open video. What applies now: the captions (on or off by how often the reference shows text, its caption height and size, over this video's caption style so its type voice stays), the look (a LUT that moves this footage's colours onto the reference's, at the recipe's strength), and the reference's transitions once they are labelled (label_transitions after analyse_reference): placed on this film's joins at the reference's rate a minute, section changes (cutaways, clip changes) before jump cuts, each only where its effect suits the join; the reply says what went where. The cut rate, zooms, ramps and tempo are the planners' (plan_cuts reads them); the reply gives them as JSON. One undo step. Starts the converge loop: then compare_to_reference.

strength.description: the look's strength (default: the recipe's, 1: the reference's look in full)

tools.name: compare_to_reference
tools.description: One round of the converge loop: renders this video small, measures it with the same pass that read the reference, and puts the two side by side (frames at the same points of each film, and drop to drop on the beat) with the diff per axis (cut rate, cuts on the beat, transitions, zooms, ramps, captions, contrast, saturation, black level, warmth, grain, tempo, the music's arc, loudness) against its tolerance. The last line is the ONE correction to make next, as the reference's absolute value: call correct_axis with it (or freeze_axis when the difference is intended), then compare again. At most six rounds; then distil_recipe. LOOK at the sheet: the numbers can't see everything.

tools.name: recipe_report
tools.description: The converge loop's diff table from its last round (no render): each axis' value on this video and on the reference, the difference against the tolerance, which are frozen or stuck, and the next correction. compare_to_reference measures a new round.

tools.name: correct_axis
tools.description: The converge loop's one correction for this round: set an axis to an ABSOLUTE value (the reference's, as compare_to_reference proposed, or your own), never a nudge. Captions and colour (captionDensity, captionPosition, captionSize, contrast, saturation, black, warmth) change the video now, as one undo step; the planner axes (shotMedian, cutsPerMinute, cutOnBeat, transitionMix, zoomPerMinute, rampPerMinute, bpm, energyArc) are recorded for the planners (plan_cuts cuts to them), except transitionMix once the reference's transitions are labelled (label_transitions): then value 0 re-deals them onto this film's joins, replacing its own transitions. grain and loudness are report only. One correction per round: then compare_to_reference again.

tools.name: freeze_axis
tools.description: Leave an axis as it is in the converge loop: the difference from the reference is intended ("our speaker is calmer than the reference"). A frozen axis is never proposed or corrected, and counts as done. off: true unfreezes it (and clears a stuck axis).

tools.name: distil_recipe
tools.description: End the converge loop: every axis that converged or was frozen writes its value from the last round back into the recipe (recipe.converged, and the recipe's own numbers for the axes it carries: shot length, cut rate, cuts on the beat, zooms, ramps, captions, the look's numbers, tempo, loudness), so the next film starts closer. Saved under the same name. Says which axes were written and which are still outside.

tools.name: study_graphics
tools.description: Study HOW a reference's graphics move, after analyse_reference (and label_transitions): every element that appears on the picture that isn't the speaker or the camera (words, stickers, badges, chat bubbles, cards, colour panels behind a cut-out speaker), found by frame differencing off the speaker's Vision mask, each timed frame by frame: when and where it enters (cut-in, pop, scale, slide, fade, blur-in, wipe), from which side, its overshoot and settle frames, how long it stays, how it leaves, its screen zone and colour, whether it sits over or behind the speaker. Shows an every-frame strip (about 0.4–0.8 s, the element outlined in red) of the most telling entrances as images (12 at most; every strip as a file) so you SEE the animation. Saves launchreel/recipes/<slug>.graphics.json beside the recipe. Then LOOK at the strips and name each element with label_graphics (kind, animation id from find_effects where one fits, cut-out pattern), then recipe_graphics gives the spec to build scenes to match. On a Mac (the speaker mask is Apple Vision; elsewhere the whole picture is searched). About a minute per minute of reference the first time.

reference.description: only this reference (1–3) of a merged recipe (default: all)

to.description: up to this second (default the end; at most 180 s a call)

tools.name: label_graphics
tools.description: Name the graphics study_graphics found, after looking at their strips: per element its kind (text, sticker, badge, panel, card, bubble, other), its animation (an effect-gallery id where one fits, e.g. "letters-rise", "soft-blur-in", "typewriter", "blur-in"; else a measured one: pop, scale, slide, fade, wipe, cut-in; else a short name of your own like "orbit"), and the cut-out pattern it uses: photo-sticker (a photo of someone cut out and stuck on), speaker-over-background (the speaker cut out over a colour, grid or picture), text-behind-speaker, circle-badge (a face in a round badge), or null. Leave out finds that aren't graphics (the footage moving). Unknown ids or kinds are refused and nothing is saved. Replaces earlier labels on the same elements (replace: true clears the rest). The per-kind specs and the summary are redone; recipe_graphics then returns them.

id.description: the element's id from study_graphics, e.g. "g4"

kind.description: text | sticker | badge | panel | card | bubble | other

anim.description: an effect-gallery id where one fits, else pop|scale|slide|fade|wipe|cut-in|blur-in or a short name (lower-case, dashes)

note.description: what you saw, in a few words (e.g. "italic serif word, black, appears as it's said")

replace.description: clear labels on elements not in this call (default: they stay)

tools.name: recipe_graphics
tools.description: The graphics spec of a recipe, to build the film's graphics to match the reference (after study_graphics and label_graphics; use it alongside use_recipe, which applies the cut, look, captions and transitions but not graphics). Returns the summary line and, as JSON, per kind (words, stickers, badges, panels, bubbles…): how many a minute, the gap between them, the animation (labelled, else measured: kind, frames, overshoot, settle frames, opacity frames, direction, blur), exits, screen zones, over/behind the speaker, colours, typical size, and the cut-out patterns used (photo-sticker → cutout_image; circle-badge → cutout_image with circle; speaker-over-background and text-behind-speaker → the cutout tool and BehindSpeaker), plus every element in brief with its time in the reference. Build scenes from it: the same kinds at the same rate in the same zones, with the same entrance timing.

tools.name: cutout_image
tools.description: Cut the main subject (a person, a face, a pet, an object) out of any still image as a PNG with transparency, for photo stickers and cut-out badges like a reference's (study_graphics/recipe_graphics name the pattern: photo-sticker, circle-badge). Apple Vision's foreground mask on the Mac, under a second. Saved in the open video's assets/stickers/.png, trimmed to the subject; circle: true also makes -circle.png, a round badge centred on the face (the photo itself, or with circleColour the cut-out subject over that colour). outline: px adds the sticker's white (or outlineColour) border all round the shape, shadow: true a soft drop shadow (the classic photo-sticker look: outline 12–24, shadow true). Use it in a scene with .png')} /> (useAsset from @launchreel/kit/scene), or as an image overlay (apply_edits addOverlay {kind: "image", src: "/assets/stickers/.png"}) — which can follow a face or a thing in the footage (follow: {seed: "face", anchor: "right", scale: true}). Returns the asset paths and a preview.

path.description: the image: an absolute path, a path relative to the repo, or an /assets/… path of this video

name.description: the sticker's name (default: the file's name)

circle.description: also make a round face badge

circleColour.description: the badge's fill behind the cut-out subject (default: the photo's own background)

outline.description: a sticker outline around the cut-out, px of the image (12–24 reads as a sticker; default none)

shadow.description: a soft drop shadow under the sticker

tools.name: save_template
tools.description: Save the open video's finished edit as a TEMPLATE the user can reuse on new footage (kept per user, in every project; the same name overwrites). It keeps the reusable part: brand colours and fonts, captions (on/off, style, and the rule for which words were marked), the look (a built-in look, or its .cube copied) and skin, the music (track or file copied, volume, fades, its volume shape), sounds by what they accompanied (an insert's entrance, a pill pop, a badge…), transitions and how many a minute, the zoom pattern and crop, cutting habits, the insert layouts and how much of the film they covered, the linked recipe and its graphics guide, and copies of the custom scenes the edit uses, each with its props schema, the props it had here and the role it played (intro, list said one by one, before/after, comparison, call to action). Footage-specific things (the recording, speaker cut-outs, word timings) are left out. Renders 2–4 poster stills for the Studio. The reply says what was captured and what was left out, and why.

name.description: what the user calls it, e.g. "Paper talk"

description.description: one line on when to use it

tools.name: list_templates
tools.description: The user's saved templates (save_template), newest first: each one's name, description, the video it came from, and in brief what it carries and which scenes.

tools.name: use_template
tools.description: Apply a saved template to the open video, normally a fresh talking head after add_footage and the cuts. Copies the template's scene files into this video's scenes/ (a clash with a different scene of the same name gets a new name), applies its brand, captions, look, skin, music, transitions (dealt onto this film's joins at the template's rate, as use_recipe does), zoom pattern and tail as ONE undo step, and returns the BUILD GUIDE: each scene's role, props schema and example props from the source edit, the sounds by role, the caption-mark rule and the graphics guide, with how to map the scenes onto this transcript (insert + anchorScene + setProp to the new words, cutout for speaker cut-outs). Then build the inserts to the guide.

tools.name: delete_template
tools.description: Delete one of the user's saved templates (its folder and copies). Videos it was applied to keep what they got.

tools.name: find_assets
tools.description: Search commercially-safe stock and icons in one call: Pexels (videos, photos), Pixabay (videos, photos, illustrations and vectors) and Iconify (icons from open sets with permissive licences). For REAL-WORLD b-roll (a city, hands typing, a crowd, nature) and icons; motion design, UI and type stay native scenes and kit blocks. Give the query in English, as what the shot shows ("rainy city street at night", not "sad"). Results are ranked for the open video's shape (portrait for 9:16, landscape for 16:9, unless you ask otherwise), each with its id (pexels:video:12345), size, length, author, licence, page and a preview URL. previews: true also shows up to 8 of their pictures. Keep one with add_asset {id} (never put a preview or provider URL in a scene). Pixabay's API has no music or sound effects: use find_music and find_sfx.

query.description: what the scene needs, in English

kind.description: video | photo | illustration | icon | any (default any)

previews.description: also show up to 8 results' preview pictures (not icons)

tools.name: add_asset
tools.description: Keep one find_assets result in the open video: downloaded (never hotlinked) into its media like an imported file (videos as b-roll in assets/broll, photos, illustrations and icons as images in assets/images, named <source>-<id>), at the size the canvas needs (the smallest that fills it, within 1080p; icons as SVG, recoloured with color). Its credit (source, author, page, licence, when) is recorded with the project automatically: get_project lists credits and the Export sheet copies them. The reply says how to place it: b-roll with add_clip role cutaway over the words it illustrates, an image as an overlay, in a scene, or as a caption icon. Adding the same result again reuses the file.

color.description: icons: the colour to draw it in, #rrggbb (one-colour sets)

tools.name: reference_board
tools.description: Read a public Pinterest board as a STYLE reference: its newest pins (up to 12, from the board's public feed) come back as pictures for you to read the palette, type, mood, texture and composition the user is after. Pins are other people's work: use them only to inform the film's own design (colours, type voice, framing, pace of detail), never place, trace or copy them into the film; they are kept in LaunchReel's cache, not in the video. For footage the film can use, find_assets.

tools.name: list_effects
tools.description: List the real compositing effects (VFX) you can add with add_effect: a label pinned to a moving thing, a mask around a subject or object, a speed ramp with frame interpolation, an impact on one word, glow / grain / halation / chromatic / lens on the footage, 3D type (behind the subject with a mask). Each kind with its params and defaults, what runs it, the checks it must pass, and what is installed here for the heavy ones. For transitions, in-shot effects, overlays and text animations use find_effects.

tools.name: add_effect
tools.description: Add a real effect to the picture (a label pinned to a moving thing, a mask around a subject or object, a speed ramp with frame interpolation, an impact on one word, glow / grain / halation / chromatic / lens, 3D type). list_effects first for kinds and params. Anchors to word ids or film seconds like an insert. Makes the track or mask it needs (a few seconds per second of video), applies the effect as one undo step, checks it (a label that leaves the frame or covers the face, a ramp out of bounds, two impacts too close are refused with the fix) and, with preview, shows it. Heavy shots (light wrap on 4K, particles, product 3D) run in Natron or Blender if installed; otherwise the reply says what to install. Then qa_report.

id.description: your id for it (unique among the effects): apply_edits setEffect/removeEffect use it

from.description: a word id, or seconds (recording seconds on a talking head)

start.description: film seconds instead of from (on a talking head they become recording seconds)

preview.description: show it (the kind's preview) after adding

tools.name: preview_effect
tools.description: See one effect the way its kind is judged: a tracked label or 3D type at its start, middle and end; a mask's cut-out over grey (six frames); a ramp or impact as a strip across it; a light effect before and after at its middle. With its check lines. Give the effect's id (get_project effects).

tools.name: list_generative_presets
tools.description: The generated-shot catalogue (Higgsfield's names where they have one): camera moves on a still of the span (crash zoom, dolly, orbit, arc, crane, bullet time, whip pan, FPV drone, handheld…), transformations (explode, melt, dissolve, morph into), restyle and b-roll from a prompt. Each with its span limits, whether the video model does it reliably or it is experimental, and which providers can run it now (this Mac with mlx-video, or the user's own fal / Replicate key). Use generated shots sparingly: a move a phone couldn't do, or b-roll the user has no footage for; never to replace a shot that exists.

tools.name: set_provider_key
tools.description: Save (or with value null remove) the user's own key for a hosted video model: fal or Replicate. Keys are stored owner-only beside the LaunchReel key, never shown again in full and never sent anywhere but that provider. Only the user's own key, given by them: never invent one. For provider "local" the value is the path of the Python that has mlx-video installed.

tools.name: install_generative_model
tools.description: Advanced: download the local video model (Wan 2.2 TI2V 5B, Apache 2.0, 8-bit MLX) for generations on this Mac. Only when the user asks to run models locally (it needs mlx-video, a Python install they do, and a multi-gigabyte download); a fal or Replicate key is the usual way. Without confirm it says the size and where it goes: ask the user, then call again with confirm: true. Call again for progress. Only Apache or MIT weights are ever downloaded.

tools.name: estimate_generation
tools.description: How long a generated shot would take and what it would cost on each provider that can run it (this Mac: time only; fal / Replicate: their list price, billed to the user's account), whether each is ready, and the cheapest and fastest. Nothing is sent.

id.description: your id for it, to change or generate it again later (omit for a new one)

from.description: a word id, or seconds (recording seconds on a talking head)

start.description: film seconds instead of from (on a talking head they become recording seconds)

provider.description: "local" (mlx-video on this Mac), "key:fal" or "key:replicate" (the user's own key)

prompt.description: b-roll: what the shot shows; others: extra direction (morphInto: what it becomes; restyle: the style)

source.description: {kind: "still", clip, at (seconds of the clip)} | {kind: "clip", clip} | {kind: "none"}; omit and the sharpest frame of the span is picked

seed.description: fixed so a retry is the same ask (default: one from the span)

target.description: morphInto: the still it becomes (an /assets/ image, or "<clip>@<seconds>")

effect.description: {from, to, provider, params: {kind, preset, prompt?, source?, seed?, resolution?}}

tools.name: preview_generation
tools.description: Before generating: the input frame the provider would start from, the full prompt and negative prompt, the provider and model, the frames, the time and the cost. Nothing is submitted. For a paid provider the reply ends with the sentence to put to the user; generate_effect with confirm: true is allowed only after their yes to this preview (within 15 minutes, for exactly this ask).

from.description: a word id, or seconds (recording seconds on a talking head)

start.description: film seconds instead of from (on a talking head they become recording seconds)

provider.description: "local" (mlx-video on this Mac), "key:fal" or "key:replicate" (the user's own key)

tools.name: generate_effect
tools.description: Generate a shot with a video model and place it over the span as b-roll (the talk keeps playing under it), colour-matched and checked; runs in the background (generation_status). preview_generation first. confirm: true only after the user has said yes to the cost shown by preview_generation; never pass it on the user's behalf. A local run (this Mac) needs no confirm. replace: true takes off the b-roll the shot covers. Generated shots are marked as generated in the project and the render log; never remove that mark.

from.description: a word id, or seconds (recording seconds on a talking head)

start.description: film seconds instead of from (on a talking head they become recording seconds)
