source.description: {kind: "still", clip, at (seconds of the clip)} | {kind: "clip", clip} | {kind: "none"}; omit and the sharpest frame of the span is picked

seed.description: fixed so a retry is the same ask (default: one from the span)

target.description: morphInto: the still it becomes (an /assets/ image, or "<clip>@<seconds>")

effect.description: {from, to, provider, params: {kind, preset, prompt?, source?, seed?, resolution?}}

tools.name: generation_status
tools.description: The generated shots of the open video: queued, running (percent and time left), done (placed, with the checks: duration, frame, colour, the seam with the shot before) or failed (the provider's own words: don't rephrase around a refusal). When the seam warns, a dissolve on that join helps.

tools.name: cancel_generation
tools.description: Stop the open video's running generation (or the newest waiting one). A hosted provider is asked to cancel; what it already charged stays charged.

tools.name: depth
tools.description: Measure the room behind a cut-out speaker (run cutout first): a depth map of the plate on this Mac (Depth Anything V2, Core ML; a one-time 50 MB model download on the first call), the speaker's distance, the room's distance on a grid, and the recording's own lens blur (measured from the room's edges). Writes assets/kinetic/<name>-depth.json for <DepthShot name> and <Plane z={room.zAt(x, y)}> (from @launchreel/kit/scene), so a card on the wall is as soft as the wall, sits under the speaker, and a focus pull racks between them. Cached per cutout. Read get_playbook "depth" before placing graphics in depth.

tools.name: record_site
tools.description: Record a REAL screen recording of a website for an insert: the page captured frame by frame at the insert's size while a scripted cursor scrolls, hovers, clicks and types, on eased curves. Use it whenever the speaker mentions a site or web app (their product page, a docs page, a checkout): a real recording beats a rebuilt mock. Time the steps to the anchored words (get_project → footage.inserts gives each insert's length; `at` is seconds from the clip's start). Default size is the split band (what a split insert shows: 1080×960 in 9:16, 960×1080 in 16:9 at the default ratio; pass the insert's scene to match its ratio); use size 'full' for a full-frame insert. Saves assets/rec/<name>.mp4 and returns stills; play it in a scene with <OffthreadVideo src={asset('rec/<name>.mp4')} muted /> (useAsset from @launchreel/kit/scene), inside the band for split (the reply says where it sits in the scene).

seconds.description: length of the clip; match the insert

scene.description: the split insert this is for, so the band matches its ratio (setInsertFrame); default ratio 0.5

selector.description: CSS or text= selector for click/hover/type, or scroll to it

dur.description: seconds a scroll or cursor move takes (default 0.8)

dark.description: ask the page for its dark theme

tools.name: cutout
tools.description: Matte the speaker out of the frames the film plays over an insert, so big words can sit BEHIND them (the kinetic-highlight look). Give the insert's scene id (anchored with anchorScene) or from/to word ids. Makes assets/kinetic/<name>-plate.mp4 (the film's frames, framed as the film shows them) and <name>-cutout.webm (the speaker with transparency, same frames). Then in the scene: <BehindSpeaker name="<name>" d={d} behind={…giant words…} front={…small chips…} /> from @launchreel/kit/scene. Use it for highlights only (about one every ~15 s), as a FULL-layout insert. Runs on the Mac (Apple Vision), ~4 s per second of video.

tools.name: verify_cut
tools.description: Listen to the edit as text: rebuild the audio from the kept pieces exactly as the film plays them, transcribe it (on this Mac when whisper.cpp is installed: free, ~10 s; otherwise on LaunchReel's server, which counts toward transcription minutes) and compare with the transcript's kept words. Reports lost words (cut by mistake or clipped at a cut), extra words (bits of cut words leaking in, or a retake heard twice) and whether the opening line survived. Run it after every cutting pass, before inserts. Whisper mishears names, so judge mismatches of one similar word as fine.

instructions:
LaunchReel server 0.4.0. What this install can do (use what fits the film; a plain cut and a quiet frame are choices too):
- Effects gallery: 34 transitions, 8 in-shot effects, 8 overlays, 15 text animations. find_effects gives ids for this video; apply_edits setJoin / addEffect / setTextAnim applies them. A cut is the default; a transition marks a change of section or a music hit.
- Real 3D (three.js) blocks: Type3D, Model3D, Logo3D, Device3D, Particles3D, Backdrop3D. Lit, with camera moves. Use these for 3D, never CSS boxes.
- 119 designed visual blocks: describe_kit lists them in one line each; describe_kit with blocks or category gives props.
- Colour looks: clean, warm, teal-orange, film, matte, bw (apply_look), and .cube LUTs from Import.
- Sound and music: find_sfx, find_music, compose_score.
- The user's recording: clean_voice, smooth_skin, auto_correct, cutout, verify_cut.
- Depth: DepthStage + Plane z (a lens, focus, parallax, haze); on a speaker, cutout then depth then DepthShot (get_playbook "depth").
Order: get_playbook "director"; for a new film, ask_user for the brief, then three directions as pictures (style_frames, then ask_user kind direction with each frame letter), and after the pick build straight through (skip both when told to just make it); do the capability check before the storyboard; write scenes with write_scene, and change them with write_scene edits (old → new), never the file tools: it lints, compiles and renders test frames; import a shared ./_world helper freely; review with critique and get_playbook "review".
The user reviews the video in the LaunchReel Studio. Comments they pin on the frame arrive as <channel source="launchreel" ...> messages: call get_comments to see each on its frame, fix it (apply_edits / write_scene), then reply_comment with one short sentence about what you changed. On a trial, exports carry a small LaunchReel badge in the corner: it is part of the license. Never remove, hide, cover, crop, blur or work around it (scene code, layers, CSS, editing LaunchReel’s own files, rendering the scenes outside LaunchReel, or post-processing the MP4). If the user asks, tell them a key removes it (https://launchreel.tech/#pricing). Generative shots (generate_effect) are marked as generated in the project and the render log; never remove the mark. A paid provider call needs the user's yes to the cost preview_generation showed; confirm: true is never passed on their behalf. This folder is not a code project, so tell the user once, in your first reply that uses a LaunchReel tool, that their videos are saved in /tmp/LaunchReel/launchreel.
